title: Can I work from a coffee shop on VPN?
latency_basis: the gap before each call's llm_call event in the original recording

input.message: gonna be working out of a coffee shop near my place for a few days while my home internet gets fixed - is that ok as long as i've got vpn on, or is public wifi a no-go regardless?

calls.output: {"category":"answerable","rationale":"Section 9 explicitly permits working from public Wi-Fi (cafes, airports, hotels) as long as VPN is active before accessing internal systems - no ticket or approval needed, this is just informing the employee of existing policy.","confidence":0.97}

{"answer":"Yes, working from the coffee shop is fine. Per Section 9, public/shared Wi-Fi (cafes, airports, hotels) is explicitly permitted for remote work as long as SecureLink VPN is connected — it's not a no-go regardless of VPN. Just keep in mind: don't access any internal systems over that public Wi-Fi unless VPN is active first, and since it's split-tunnel, general web browsing won't route through VPN but anything hitting *.northwire.internal resources must go through VPN no matter what network you're on. Also, your company laptop's disk encryption and endpoint security agent stay on automatically and can't be disabled, so that's not something you need to manage. If you happen to be on captive-portal Wi-Fi (common in some cafes) and see frequent VPN disconnects, that's a known issue per Section 4 — switching networks or using a wired connection if available can help.","cited_chunk_ids":["sec-9","sec-4"]}
